record.original_question: Let L be an infinite homogeneous linearly ordered topological space. If a compact Hausdorff space X is cleavable over L, must X be embeddable into L?

evidence.quote: Question 7 (Buzyakova). Is a compact Hausdorff space X that is cleavable over an infinite homogeneous LOTS L must be embeddable in L?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Recall that a topological space $X$ is said to be cleavable over a space $Y$ if for every subset $A \subseteq X$ there exists a continuous function $f : X \to Y$ such that $f(A) \cap f(X \setminus A) = \emptyset$. A linearly ordered topological space (LOTS) is a linearly ordered set endowed with the topology generated by its open intervals. A topological space $L$ is homogeneous if for any two points $p, q \in L$ there is a homeomorphism of $L$ onto itself sending $p$ to $q$.

Question: Let $L$ be an infinite homogeneous linearly ordered topological space, and let $X$ be a compact Hausdorff space that is cleavable over $L$. Must $X$ be homeomorphic to a subspace of $L$?
artifact.status_search_result: Related results by Buzyakova and others establish embeddability of compacta cleavable over ordinals and over certain scattered or separable LOTS under additional hypotheses, but a definitive resolution of the question for arbitrary infinite homogeneous LOTS does not appear in the located sources. The status of this specific question could not be conclusively verified.

status_evidence.title: On cleavability of continua over LOTS
status_evidence.snippet: Results on cleavability of compacta over linearly ordered topological spaces, with partial embeddability conclusions under extra hypotheses.
status_evidence.claim: Related partial results are known but the homogeneous LOTS case is not resolved in this source.

status_evidence.title: Cleavability and scattered sets of non-trivial fibers
status_evidence.snippet: Conditions under which an infinite compactum cleavable over a separable LOTS is itself a LOTS.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress on cleavability-to-embeddability questions exists but does not settle the homogeneous case.
